entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: :   A naturally occurring compound found in foods such as wheat germ, mushrooms, and aged cheese may help older adults build stronger protection after vaccination. In a small pilot trial, researchers gave spermidine supplements to adults over 65 following their third COVID-19 vaccine dose. A naturally occurring compound called spermidine may help strengthen vaccine responses in some older adults by reducing biological signs of immune system aging, according to research published in *Aging Cell*. The immune system becomes less efficient as people grow older, making it harder for the body to fight infections and respond fully to vaccines. This gradual decline, known as immunosenescence, can increase vulnerability to age-related health problems and leave some older adults with weaker protection after vaccination. Their findings suggest that taking a daily spermidine supplement improved several measures of immune response following COVID-19 vaccination. entity_ranked_evidence.title: US sees highest number of measles cases in 35 years - BBC
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: The US has hit a 35-year high in measles cases, according to new figures from the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC). The US has seen 2,318 confirmed cases of measles in 2026, just seven months into the year, up from last year's high of 2,289, when two unvaccinated children died of the disease. The rising number of cases have come as vaccine hesitancy in the US has increased in recent years, leading to lower immunisation rates. The US has recorded more measles cases over the past 18 months than the total number over 25 years before that. Over the past month, Virginia and Pennsylvania have been dealing with new measles outbreaks, while the state of Utah is still responding to a cluster of infections that began last year. Earlier this year, a federal judge blocked the US government from implementing a series of sweeping changes to childhood immunisations under Kennedy's leadership, including slashing the number of recommended shots for children from 17 to 11.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: GSK's Shingrix (Recombinant Zoster Vaccine) prefilled syringe presentation approved in Canada - BioSpace
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # GSK’s Shingrix (Recombinant Zoster Vaccine) prefilled syringe presentation approved in Canada. MISSISSAUGA, ON, July 24, 2026 /CNW/ -- GSK Canada today announced the approval of *Shingrix* (GSK's Recombinant Zoster Vaccine or RZV) in a prefilled syringe. Consistent with the existing indications for *Shingrix*, the prefilled syringe is licensed in Canada for the prevention of shingles in adults 50 years of age or older, as well as those 18 years of age or older who are or will be at increased risk of shingles due to immunodeficiency or immunosuppression caused by known disease or therapy. *Shingrix* combines an antigen, glycoprotein E, with an adjuvant system, AS01B, and may help overcome the natural age-related decline in responses to immunization that contributes to the challenge of protecting adults aged 50 and over from shingles, as well as those 18 years of age or older who are or will be at increased risk of shingles due to immunodeficiency or immunosuppression caused by known disease or therapy.

entity_ranked_evidence.title: US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC - ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
entity_ranked_evidence.snippet: # US measles cases hit 2,318 in 2026, surpassing last year's total: CDC. This marks the highest number of cases recorded since 1991. The number of confirmed measles cases in the U.S. so far this year has hit 2,318, surpassing the total reported for all last year, according to data updated Friday from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Previously, last year's total of 2,289 was the highest number of recorded measles cases in more than 30 years, CDC data shows. Sixteen of this year's total have been among international visitors to the U.S., according to the CDC. The majority of measles cases in 2026 have been confirmed among children and teenagers aged 19 and younger, according to the CDC. Meanwhile, 3% of cases are among those who have received just one dose of the measles, mumps, rubella (MMR) vaccine and 4% of cases are among those who received the recommended two doses, according to the CDC.
